title: Administrator / Legal Secretary Re-train Opportunity
description:
Job Title: Legal Secretary Re-train Opportunity

Location: Sharston, M22 4 SN

Salary: £28,000 Per annum

Job type: Full time, Permanent

Established in 2000, Express Solicitors is an award-winning, no win no fee law firm specialising exclusively in personal injury claims. Headquartered in Manchester, we support clients nationwide across all areas of personal injury, including employers' liability, serious injury, clinical negligence, occupiers' and public liability, road traffic accidents and industrial disease.

We are ranked 60th in The Lawyer UK Top 200, out of more than 10,000 law firms nationwide, and after achieving a 24% year-on-year growth, Express Solicitors are the largest personal injury claimant firm in the UK.

Our commitment to outstanding client care is reflected in our Trustpilot rating of 4.7 (Excellent), placing us among the highest-rated firms in the sector.

About The Role:

We are currently looking for strong administrators ideally with a minimum of two years administration experience. Background in legal and medical advantageous

Following extensive training you will be working in a pool of Legal Secretaries assisting a number of Lawyers. The job is varied with not just typing and file management, but preparing bundles, taking and making calls to clients, arranging meetings & conferences.

Responsibilities
- Working collaboratively within a pool of Legal Secretaries to support multiple Lawyers
- You will be working in one stream of work either Road Traffic Accidents, Employers' Liability or Occupiers & Public Liability.
- Preparing correspondence and legal documentation, including pleadings and court bundles
- Photocopying and scanning documents, with support from the Administration team where required
- Handling inbound and outbound telephone calls in a professional and courteous manner
- Scheduling appointments, arranging meetings, and liaising with Lawyers, clients, Counsel, and other stakeholders
- Providing support to fellow Legal Secretaries and the wider administration team as required
- Assisting with updates to the Proclaim case management system where appropriate

Person Specification:
- Demonstrable two years previous administration experience, background in legal and medical advantageous.
- Strong comprehension of English spelling, punctuation, and grammar.
- IT literate
- Exceptional customer service skills, including professional and friendly telephone manner.
- Acute attention to detail
- Ability to prioritise daily workload and experience of working in a fast-paced environment.
- Prior exposure to Proclaim case management system is desirable.
- Excellent word processing and audio typing skills
- Audio typing speed of 65+ words per minute
- Use of digital dictation, ideally Diktamen would be beneficial.

Salary & Hours
- A basic salary of up to £28,000
- Our standard working hours are 8:30am to 5:30pm Monday-Thursday and 8:30am to 5pm Friday.

Benefits:
- Hybrid Working - 3/2 hybrid working pattern after probation.
- 23 Days Holiday - Rising to 26 days, plus bank/public holidays.
- Extra Holidays - 3 holiday buy backs and an extra day for your birthday after service length requirement.
- Looking After Your Health - Private medical insurance available after 2 years' service, annual flu jab and Employee Assistance Programme.
- Looking After Your Well-being - 24/7 onsite Gym, Netball/Football team, 10km Manchester team and more.
- Work Life / Balance - Active social committee with generous departmental and firm-wide social budget.

Recruitment Process:

Interviews will be conducted by MS Teams and will include scenario-based questioning.

Our employees are our most important asset, we rate skill and ability above all else and our recruitment policy encourages applications from all.

Please click APPLY to be redirected to our website to complete your application.

Candidates with the relevant experience or job titles of; Legal Secretary, PA, Legal Typist, Typist, Legal PA, Secretary, Legal Administrator, Legal Office Support, Legal Assistant, Legal Business Support, Office Administrator, Business Support Admin Assistant may also be considered For This Role.

title: Claims Against Public Authorities Paralegal
description:
Duncan Lewis Solicitors:

Regulated by the Solicitor's Regulation Authority, Duncan Lewis Solicitors was founded in 1998 and is headquartered in the City of London (Fenchurch Street EC3 M), with offices nationwide. We are recognised by the Legal 500 and Chambers & Partners UK independent legal directories as a top-tier law firm in all of our key practice areas - "a diligent and professional team that is prepared to go the extra mile for its clients". A paperless law firm with over 500 personnel that embraces hybrid-working, we service both corporate entities and private individuals in over 25 areas of law across 60 languages. We give people a voice - that is our ethos.

Recognised among The Times 200 Best Law Firms, we have been awarded Law Firm of the Year at the 2024 Lexis Nexis Awards and 2023 Modern Law Awards, reflecting our dedication to legal expertise and client service. We hold Investors in People Gold Standard accreditation for over 15 years, showcasing our commitment to professional development. Duncan Lewis is also Law Society Lexcel, Cyber Essentials Plus, and ISO 27001 certified, ensuring excellence in practice management and data security.

We are committed to recruiting dedicated and talented professionals and welcome applications from exceptional candidates. At Duncan Lewis, we value training and diversity, and we take pride in our inclusive workforce.

About the role:

Duncan Lewis Solicitors is seeking a talented and experienced paralegals to join its Claims Against Public Authorities department

The successful candidate will conduct supervised casework and also support other lawyers in the department. You will be involved with case preparation generally and, as part of that role, will be expected to conduct legal research, take proofs of evidence from clients and witnesses, attend both court hearings and conferences

Experience of Legal Aid Agency (LAA) funded casework is highly desirable. Previous CAPA and/or Inquest experience is advantageous.

It is imperative that you can demonstrate an unwavering commitment to protecting individual citizens' civil liberties and a preparedness to fight hard to enforce their human rights. While experience in CAPA work is advantageous, applications from candidates with relevant legal experience and a genuine interest in civil liberties and human rights work will also be considered.

Main Responsibilities of the Role:
- Reporting to Supervising Solicitor and when necessary to Departmental Director
- Working cohesively within a team but also prepared to take responsibility for individual work.
- Attending clients, taking instructions and briefing and liaising with counsel, negotiating with defendant solicitors, the PPO, IOPC and other legal professionals.
- Drafting legal documents.
- Exercising financial control over work carried out, with particular regard to the conversion of work in progress and ensuring that billing targets are met.
- Ensuring Quality Control compliance as defined in the Office Manual in regard to Lexcel, Investors in People and any other quality mark implemented by the firm, dealing with non-compliance matters in an efficient and timely fashion.
- Supporting the successful development of the firm, in line with its Business Plan, this will require participation in marketing events to ensure the continuous growth of the Department, and that the turnover target set for your department is achieved.
- Dealing with any complaints received on your cases.
- Assisting with audit enquiries, when applicable
- Carrying out any other reasonable and relevant task required by Management

Key Skills Required:
- Minimum 1 year of paralegal practice required; experience in a claims against public authorities department is highly desirable.
- Intelligence and demonstrable experience relevant to this role
- A strong interest in Claims Against Public Authorities (CAPA) work, with the ambition to develop into a Trainee Solicitor and, in due course, qualify as a CAPA Solicitor.
- Experience working on Legal Aid cases and Litigation is essential (Ideally within Inquests/CAPA)
- Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks and manage time effectively
- Familiarity with the Legal Aid Agency's online CCMS system would be an advantage
- Legal skills and knowledge, Negotiation skills and Analytical skills
- You must be a good administrator, capable of ordering documents, dealing with new telephone and email enquiries and completing legal aid/controlled work documentation.

What we offer:
- Competitive salary
- The opportunity to join a heavyweight civil liberties firm which promotes a healthy collegiate environment in which to do great work, grow, be supported and be yourself
- Work within a friendly, collaborative and cohesive team
- Excellent progression opportunities
- Support for appropriate legal awards/recognition

The recruitment process will fully comply with GDPR and other applicable laws. Background checks including CRB / DBS checks will establish your eligibility to work in the UK and suitability to the role.

Equal Opportunities:

Duncan Lewis is committed to Equal Opportunities and embraces diversity of its staff. The Company strives to ensure that our staff reflects the diversity of the communities we serve, which is reflective at all levels within our workforce.

We guarantee an interview for candidates that disclose a disability and meet the essential requirements for the post. Please provide additional details in your covering letter if this applies.

title: Health and Welfare Court of Protection Paralegal
company: Simpson Millar LLP Solicitors - Agency - Permanent
description:
To provide legal and administrative support to solicitors handling Court of Protection Health and Welfare matters and ensuring clients receive high-quality, compassionate, and effective legal representation.

A Health and Welfare Court of Protection Paralegal may assist with matters involving:
- Best interests decisions
- Deprivation of Liberty (DoLS and Liberty Protection Safeguards-related matters)
- Residence and care disputes
- Contact with family members
- Medical treatment decisions
- Serious medical treatment applications
- Safeguarding concerns
- Mental capacity assessments
- Challenges to local authority or NHS decisions.

This is a rewarding area of law that combines legal analysis with direct client interaction, advocacy, and multidisciplinary working to protect the rights and welfare of vulnerable individuals.

Key Responsibilities
- Assisting solicitors with a caseload of Health and Welfare Court of Protection matters.
- Drafting court applications, witness statements, legal correspondence, attendance notes, and court bundles.
- Liaising with clients, family members, advocates, social workers, healthcare professionals, local authorities, and other agencies.
- Attending client meetings in hospitals, care homes, supported living settings, or clients' homes.
- Assisting with preparing cases for hearings and conferences with counsel.
- Managing files, maintain accurate records, and comply with regulatory and file management procedures.
- Monitoring court deadlines and ensure timely filing of documents.
- Handling new enquiries and assist with client onboarding.
- Supporting applications for legal aid where appropriate.
- Assisting with business development activities, networking, and maintaining professional relationships.
- Conducting legal research on relevant legislation and case law, including; The Mental Capacity Act 2005, The Mental Health Act 1983, The Care Act 2014 and Human rights and safeguarding law.

Key Requirements:
- Law degree, Graduate Diploma in Law (GDL), or equivalent legal qualification.
- Must have at least 12 months experience assisting with Health & welfare Court of Protection matters
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong organisational and time management abilities.
- High attention to detail.
- Ability to work empathetically with vulnerable clients.
- Professionalism, discretion, and confidentiality.
- Competent in Microsoft Office and legal case management systems.
- Excellent knowledge of legal aid procedures.
- Experience attending court or client meetings.

At Simpson Millar, you'll be part of a people-focused firm that is committed to delivering exceptional client care while supporting the development and wellbeing of its colleagues. We offer all level 2 employees:

title: Paralegal
description:
Paralegal - Trade Union Law Group

Paralegal Employment Law Litigation Trade Unions Social Justice Career Development

Looking for a Paralegal role where you can work on landmark cases, develop specialist litigation expertise and make a genuine difference to working people's lives?

Join Thompsons Solicitors' nationally recognised Trade Union Law Group (TULG), the trusted legal adviser to many of the UK's leading trade unions. As the UK's foremost social justice law firm, we act in pioneering cases that shape employment and trade union law. Recent successes include Tesco Stores Ltd v USDAW, where we secured a landmark injunction preventing Tesco's controversial "fire and rehire" proposals and protecting the rights of thousands of workers.

We will consider full or part time applicants.

The Role

As a Paralegal, you'll support highly experienced trade union lawyers on complex and high-profile matters, including:
- High Court and appellate litigation
- Judicial Review proceedings
- Multi-claimant Employment Tribunal cases
- Large-scale group actions involving thousands of claimants
- Strategic cases that influence employment and collective rights law

This is an exceptional opportunity to gain exposure to challenging, meaningful legal work while building a long-term career within one of the UK's most respected claimant law firms.

What We're Looking For
- Aspiring solicitor or legal professional with a strong interest in employment and trade union law
- Litigation experience or knowledge of court procedures (desirable)
- Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills
- Strong IT and Microsoft Excel capability
- Confident communicator with clients and stakeholders
- Ability to manage competing priorities effectively
- Commitment to social justice and the values of the trade union movement

What We Offer

- Contributory pension scheme

title: Conveyancing Assistant - Prestwich
description:
Conveyancing Assistant - Prestwich
Salary: Up to £28,000 DOE
Working Pattern: Full-Time, Permanent

An excellent opportunity has arisen for an experienced Conveyancing Assistant to join a well-established law firm in Prestwich. This is an ideal opportunity for a Conveyancing Assistant or Residential Property Paralegal looking to develop their career within a supportive team, working alongside experienced property fee earners and assisting with a varied caseload of residential conveyancing transactions.

The firm has an established presence across Greater Manchester and provides a range of legal services to individuals and businesses. Its residential property team advises clients throughout the buying and selling process, with a strong emphasis on clear communication, efficient transaction management and excellent client care.

This position would suit someone who already has experience in residential conveyancing and is looking for a stable, long-term opportunity within an established property department.

The Role You will provide essential support to the residential conveyancing team, assisting with the progression of property transactions from initial instruction through to completion and post-completion.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Assisting with residential property sales and purchases.
- Supporting freehold and leasehold conveyancing transactions.
- Assisting with remortgages and transfers of equity.
- Opening files, preparing client care documentation and completing initial administrative tasks.
- Preparing contract packs, transfer deeds and other conveyancing documentation.
- Obtaining property searches and assisting with pre-contract enquiries.
- Liaising with clients, estate agents, mortgage lenders and other solicitors to keep transactions progressing.
- Monitoring key dates, maintaining accurate case records and chasing outstanding documentation.
- Assisting with exchange and completion arrangements.
- Supporting post-completion work, including Land Registry applications and related documentation.
- Providing regular updates to clients and helping to ensure a smooth and efficient transaction process.

You will play an important role in the day-to-day running of the department, helping fee earners manage their workloads and ensuring clients receive a professional and responsive service throughout their property transactions.

Requirements
- Previous experience in a residential conveyancing assistant, conveyancing paralegal or similar legal support role.
- A good understanding of the residential conveyancing process from instruction through to completion.
- Experience supporting property sales, purchases and remortgages.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office and familiarity with legal case management systems.
- Excellent attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate records.
- A proactive approach to chasing outstanding information and progressing transactions.
- A professional, approachable manner with a strong commitment to client care.
- The ability to work independently while contributing positively to a busy team.

Benefits
- Salary of up to £28,000, depending on experience.
- Full-time, permanent position.
- Opportunity to join an established residential property team.
- Supportive and collaborative working environment.
- Exposure to a varied caseload of residential property transactions.
- Opportunities to develop your conveyancing knowledge and progress your career.
- Additional benefits package.

- Providing day-to-day secretarial support to solicitors and fee earners, helping them manage their workload efficiently
- Preparing legal documents, contracts, correspondence and other paperwork as required
- Maintaining client files and ensuring documents and records are accurate and up to date
- Supporting the administration of legal matters and helping keep cases progressing.
- Answering incoming calls, dealing with client enquiries and passing on messages where needed
- Covering reception, welcoming visitors and providing a professional first point of contact
- Assisting with general office administration and supporting colleagues across the team when required

What's in it for you?
- 14.50- 16.50 per hour, depending on experience.
- Flexible part-time options: work two days per week, Monday and Tuesday, or add Friday to make it three days.
- 14 hours per week minimum, with the option to work 21 hours.
- Consistent working hours: 9am-5pm, with a one-hour lunch break.
- Weekly pay and holiday pay during the temporary assignment.
- Smart-casual dress code in a professional working environment.
- Potential for a permanent position, depending on business requirements and suitability.

Why would you join this company?
You'll be supporting an established legal team where good organisation, accurate administration and dependable secretarial support are valued.
The role offers a varied working day, combining legal secretarial responsibilities with client contact and general office support. With the choice of two or three working days, it's an opportunity to continue using your legal experience while working a part-time schedule.
What we're looking for
What's essential:
- Previous experience working as a Legal Secretary within a law firm or legal environment
- Experience preparing documents, managing files and providing secretarial support to solicitors or fee earners
- Good IT skills, including confidence using Microsoft Word and other Microsoft Office applications
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail
- The ability to manage a varied workload and prioritise tasks effectively
- Professional communication skills when dealing with clients over the telephone and face-to-face
- Availability to work on Mondays and Tuesdays

What's helpful but not essential:
- Previous experience as a Conveyancing Legal Secretary
- Experience with residential property transactions and conveyancing documentation, whether recently or earlier in your career
- Experience in another area of law, with transferable legal secretarial skills and the confidence to learn new processes
- Previous reception or general office administration experience
- Availability to work Fridays as well, if you'd prefer three days per week

You don't need to be working in conveyancing right now. We're keen to hear from experienced Legal Secretaries who have conveyancing knowledge from earlier in their career, as well as those currently supporting solicitors in other areas of law. The key is having a solid legal secretarial background and being available on Mondays and Tuesdays.
The Essentials
Salary: 14.50- 16.50 per hour, depending on experience
Hours: Two days per week minimum (Monday and Tuesday), 9am-5pm, with a one-hour lunch break. The option to add Friday for three days per week
Working hours: 14 hours per week minimum, or 21 hours if working Monday, Tuesday and Friday
Location: Didsbury
Job type: Temporary, with the potential to become permanent
To Apply
If you're an experienced Legal Secretary looking for part-time hours and have a background in conveyancing or another area of law, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Litigation Executive/Paralegal - Recoveries Department
description:
Litigation Executive - Recoveries Department

Onsite - Media City, Salford Quays (Manchester)

Permanent

Following a Road Traffic Accident, HF's recoveries team are instructed by insurance companies to determine liability and then recover uninsured losses and insurer's outlay from third parties. HF has been undertaking recoveries work for clients for a number of years and the team have a great reputation due to their specialist industry experience securing many millions of pounds per annum for clients

We know it's you who makes the difference.

Paralegal, Litigation Executive, File Handler, Legal Negotiator, Legal Support, Legal Admin, Legal Advisor, Litigation Support, Litigation Paralegal, no matter what your title is, it's a great time to join HF Recoveries. Our success is breeding success. So, if you are ambitious and hardworking then you can be part of something exciting as we grow and develop together.

If you want to move your career onto your next level, then please read on.

HF Recoveries are recruiting for a Litigation Executive, and we can offer you a long and rewarding career in Litigation. HF Recoveries are renowned for our claimant work, but did you know we also manage defendant files too, from small claims track, to fast track, and onto Intermediate track up to high value multi track work.

We are looking for talented people to help our impressive list of client insurers. If you are confident, you can support our Clients and their Policyholders through the litigation process to recover their outstanding outlay and uninsured losses, then we'd like to hear from you.

We can help you kick start your legal career by training you in all aspects of RTA Recoveries litigation, and if you have legal experience, we can help you to develop and hone your Litigation expertise. No matter what stage your career is at, we can offer you outstanding opportunities and training.

No day is the same in HF Recoveries, our Litigation Executives are legal experts, who have a keen sense of commercial awareness, present the facts, the law, and have a track record of successfully negotiating great outcomes for our Clients and Policyholders, in a reasoned and persuasive manner.

If you are hardworking, well organised, enjoy working as part of a successful team, have a confident telephone manner and enjoy being flexible and creative when it comes to tackling new litigation challenges, then we would like to hear from you.

What you'll be doing
- Drafting court documents, proceedings and applications
- Manage a litigated caseload
- Obtain and draft witness statements
- Review third party evidence
- Instruct Counsel
- Manage client expectations
- Resolution of liability disputes
- Resolution of Quantum disputes
- Issuing County Court proceedings
- Adhere to Court directions and deadlines
- Take initiative to suggest ideas for improvements and understand the value of different working ideas
- Work to set priorities, create clear plans and manage all work to meet the needs of the client

What do I need?

This opportunity would suit an ambitious individual looking to take the next step in their legal career. We are seeking someone with a can-do attitude, a desire to learn and grow, and the determination to demonstrate their potential and make a real impact.
- Previous experience within a similar role handling a case load.- Desirable
- A knowledge or experience of RTA liability - Desirable
- Previous experience working within the insurance sector - Desirable
- Experience of working in a fast paced environment. - Desirable.
- Ability to interpret and input data accurately and efficiently. - Essential
- Ability to demonstrate initiative. - Essential
- Professional and confident telephone manner - Essential

Personal Attributes:
- Enthusiastic and self-motivated individual with a desire to achieve and exceed targets.
- Ability to work and thrive in a busy environment working well under pressure.
- High levels of attention to detail.
- Strong work ethic and a committed team player.

What's in it for you?

Quite A Lot Really.

We offer attractive salaries as well as hybrid and flexible working hours, once you have successfully passed your 6 months' probation period.

We want your career to flourish, and we will continually invest in you, offering you lots of training and support.

We're always looking to recognise and reward our people and here are just a few of the benefits you'll have access to, as part of our team:
- 25 days' annual leave (in addition to public holidays), increasing to 30 days with long service
- Private healthcare provision
- Company pension scheme
- Enhanced parental leave
- Cycle to Work scheme
- Life insurance and income protection
- Employee Assistance Programme & Digital GP service
- Season ticket loans
- Flu vouchers
- Bonus scheme
- HF Discount Hub
- Free Parking

Who are we?

We know it's you the person that counts

HF is one of the UK's leading providers of legal and handling services to the insurance and commercial sectors. Established in 1969, the firm currently provides legal services to 12 of the UK's 20 largest insurers in specialist areas such as Counter Fraud, Large & Catastrophic Injury, Motor, Disease, Casualty, Aviation, Recoveries, Costs and Credit Hire.

Over the past 5 years, HF has expanded rapidly, significantly investing in it's people and adding commercial services to our traditional insurance client base.

We are an ambitious , independent, national law firm which genuinely does things differently with a forward thinking innovative approach that's built around our clients' needs - not our own!

Sounds great? What next?

If you are ready to apply, press the button is below and we look forward to hearing from you.

As an equal opportunities' employer, we're passionate about inclusive hiring approaches.

When you apply, you'll be asked about any adjustments you might need to support the recruitment process. Let us know, and we'll do our best to support you.

Please note you will have to complete your induction, onboarding and 6 months training from our Media City office in Manchester.
